summary.intent: Resume the callisto-hardening follow-up work: upgrade CI macOS runners off the retired macos-14, clean up stale branches and worktrees, diagnose and fix the broken Release workflow, and ship the version-checkpoint resume feature (PR #546) with its review findings resolved.
summary.outcome: macOS runners moved to macos-15 (#421, merged) then macos-latest (#422, draft), 22 stale worktrees and branches cleaned, the release failure traced to a stale release PR (E165) with a revert PR and trail created, and the checkpoint PR trimmed to drop --abort, fixing the sibling-workspace finding and two further findings. Final local checks were still being re-run, and the last fixes were not yet pushed.

repo: Release workflow fails with E165 ('no changeset was consumed by this commit') when a release PR merges after changesets on main were rewritten; every later push to main retries the same stale release and fails.
Entire opens a draft PR automatically when a trail is created and the branch is linked, so use `gh pr edit` rather than `gh pr create`.

Entire Gates is the check that fails on open review findings; Entire re-reviews each new head and sets resolved/stale itself, and the default finding list hides stale ones unless `--freshness any` is passed.
Git commits in this repo are GPG-signed; the sandbox blocks GPG, `entire`, `gh` and ssh-agent access, so those commands need to run outside it.
`testing/check-comments.sh` (part of `just lint`) can fail even when clippy is clean; `just workflow-contracts` validates workflow and action script changes.
docs/specs/versioning.json criterion IDs (VER-APPLY-N) can collide when main gains new ones while a branch is open; the checkpoint criteria were renumbered to 19 and 20.

ADR 2 (committed decision verified against the merge commit) and ADR 3 (reruns adopt what already landed) cover release races and partial failures; persisted version-apply checkpoints were deferred on 2026-10-30 with a revisit condition of 'only if failures recur'.
ubuntu-24.04-arm has no -latest label, so it stays pinned; all other runners use *-latest.

code.finding: macOS artifact preflight matrix entries pinned runner: macos-14, later macos-15, then macos-latest; callisto-release.yml has the same pins at lines 297 and 302.

CheckpointFacts now records the workspace path so a checkpoint from a sibling workspace is treated as a changed input and refused with E340; abort-only primitives (is_ignored, unstage, created_since, untracked_files) were removed.
analyze_resume and ResumeAnalysis were reduced to resume_input_changes, since abort analysis was removed.
Tests were verified by mutation: temporarily removing each fix makes exactly its new test fail. Error help text is wrapped by the renderer, so assertions must normalise whitespace.

workflow: Check recorded decisions (`entire brain recall`) before designing a feature; the checkpoint had already been weighed and deferred, and the earlier recall used different wording and missed it.
Resolve or address review findings locally before pushing, since each push triggers a re-review and the open count can grow; the user explicitly required this.
Triage review findings as input, not obligations: when one sub-feature (--abort) produced most findings across three rounds, cutting the feature beat patching it.
Don't make product decisions silently (such as how a refused resume gets undone); ask the user, and when corrected, narrow scope instead of widening.
Confirm evidence that a problem actually occurs before building (about 2,200 lines were spent on a failure no user had reported).
Pasting `! cmd` with a placeholder or after other text reaches the assistant as plain text and does not run; it must be the entire prompt with a real value.
Merge commits from GitHub show signature status 'E' locally because the web-flow key is not in the local keyring; this is not unsigned.

friction: Entire search and auth were blocked by sandbox TLS and proxy errors until the user ran `! entire auth status` themselves.
The Entire session title did not match the name the user used ('callisto-hardening'); the session had to be found by scanning local transcripts.
GPG signing, gh token minting (OpenSSL 'unsupported' error on the bot key), the ssh-agent and the GitHub changelog fetch were all blocked or failed in the sandbox.

The assistant sank a day and about 2,200 lines into the checkpoint with --abort and repeated review rounds; the user stopped it with 'STOP RUSHING' and later had to correct it twice on 'resolve before pushing'.
The assistant wrongly claimed three open findings would go stale; Entire's re-review showed they were real defects.
The assistant made several edits and deletions (half-trim) before walking the user through what was real versus over-engineered.
`just lint` failed on the comment checker after the last edits, requiring a follow-up fix.
The macos-14 retirement date was never confirmed against GitHub's changelog.
open_items: Trail #159 (macOS 15 move) is still open though #421 merged; the worktree for it also still needs cleanup.
PR #422 (macos-latest) needs CI results and the user's approval of trail #160 in Entire.

Revert PR for the stale release commit 9148c135 needs to merge, then the release PR regenerates; the guard against merging a stale release PR, the cause of the failed release-PR refresh on the #420 push, and the stray `callisto-graph@0` SemVer warnings still need investigating.

PR #546 needs the latest fixes pushed (the two extra findings), Entire's re-review, user approval, and ADR 13 updated to cite the user's incident once they say whether it was a `version` or `release` interruption.
Remote branches for merged PRs were left in place, and several local worktrees and branches (smoke-main, wf_cd627354-1a0-2, callisto-homebrew-tap, stack/docs-v1) await a user decision.
Many audit-fix and release trails remain open in Entire and need an audit.
Spec drift re-verification, #290 guard gaps, the E194 shared tag title, T12 registry tests, matrix.rs triples, npm OIDC trusted publishing and the `ready_by_edge` swap remain from the original plan.
The `uses: $/.github/actions/...` actionlint warning in both workflows is unexplained.
